sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose note and imports
sections.what: Explains that this script tests the E14 gate's maths, logic and refusal rules without a database or network. It pulls in the statistics functions, the validator and the shared types.
sections.why: The header explains why the instrument must be checked before its readings are believed.
sections.watch_out: If the imported module names or paths change, this script stops working before any check runs.

sections.name: check
sections.title: Pass or fail recorder
sections.what: Prints one line per check and counts failures. A failed check shows the value obtained and the value expected.
sections.why: Lets every check run and report, instead of stopping at the first failure.
sections.watch_out: Only the failure count sets the exit code, so any new check must go through this function.

sections.name: near
sections.title: Textbook value checks
sections.what: Compares the statistics outputs with published values, such as the inverse normal of 0.975 and a worked Newcombe example, within a small tolerance.
sections.why: Shows the maths matches published references before the gate's logic is tested.
sections.watch_out: The tolerance allows small differences, so a subtle error in the maths could still pass.

sections.name: CRIT
sections.title: Single test criterion
sections.what: Defines one criterion, a pillar named Fixture pillar, that every fake project is scored against.
sections.why: Keeps each test about one measured item so results are easy to read.
sections.watch_out: The id P1 is used in the fake project records, so changing it means changing those records too.

sections.name: group
sections.title: Fake project group builder
sections.what: Makes fake projects for one outcome, with set counts of met, not-met and unknown results. Unknown results get zero facts, and the others get 25.
sections.why: Lets each test set the exact mix of results it needs.
sections.watch_out: The zero fact count on unknown results is what marks them as unknown, so changing it changes how they are treated.

sections.name: run (part 1)
sections.title: Core verdict tests
sections.what: Runs the validator on fake groups. It checks that unknown results are left out of the denominator and reported separately, and that the effect survives that exclusion. It also checks the negative control and that the discriminates, does-not-discriminate and two early refusal paths can happen.
sections.why: The file calls the unknown rule the control that matters most, because counting unknowns as not-met would erase a real effect.
sections.watch_out: Expected results depend on the default values in the parameter set, so changing those defaults can break these tests.

sections.name: run (part 2)
sections.title: Refusal and parameter tests
sections.what: Checks that the underpowered, boundary-spanning and no-variation refusals can happen. It also checks that changing the minimum group size and minimum effect parameters actually changes the verdict.
sections.why: Proves each refusal reason is reachable and that the thresholds are read from parameters rather than fixed in code.
sections.watch_out: These tests use specific group sizes that only fall into each refusal band under the current thresholds.

sections.name: run (part 3)
sections.title: Full report shape check
sections.what: Runs the validator on one strong split and checks the parameter tag, group sizes, refusal counts, and that both the p-value and the interval appear in the output.
sections.why: Confirms the report carries the information a reader needs, and that the p-value is shown alongside the interval, not in place of it.
sections.watch_out: The expected parameter tag string must be changed whenever the parameter set is versioned.

summary: Self-test for the E14 statistical gate, which decides whether a rubric criterion separates projects that overran from those that did not.
purpose: Proves the gate can produce each of its possible answers before anyone trusts a reading from it.
why: The file header says a gate that reports nothing discriminating looks the same as a broken gate, so the instrument itself must be checked first.
how: First it checks the statistics against published textbook values. Then it builds fake project groups and checks the unknown-value rule, including a negative control where folding unknowns into not-met should erase the effect. Then it checks that every verdict and refusal reason can happen, that thresholds are read from parameters, and that the full report has the expected shape.
inputs: No inputs from outside. It uses built-in fixtures, the statistics module, the validator, and the parameter set.
outputs: A line per check labelled PASS or FAIL, with the value obtained. A final summary line. The process exits 0 if everything passes and 1 otherwise.
risks: Passing only shows the logic works on made-up data. It says nothing about whether real project records are correct. Unexpected errors are not caught, so a crash stops the run rather than being reported as a check.
debug: Run npx tsx script/verify-e14.ts from the api-server folder. Find the first FAIL line, which shows the value got and the value wanted. If a statistics check fails, look at the stats module first. If only verdict checks fail, look at the parameter defaults, since many expected results depend on them.
